text.en: After lunch Raju asked, "Where does my food go?" His teacher drew a long tube from the mouth to the anus.

Digestion includes mechanical breakdown and chemical breakdown. Enzymes help turn many large food molecules into smaller substances that the body can absorb. The alimentary canal is the passage from the mouth to the anus. Teeth are of different types, and the dental formula shows how many of each type are in one half of each jaw.
The small intestine has three main sections: the duodenum, jejunum and ileum. Much digestion is completed there, and most nutrient absorption happens there. The liver makes bile, which is delivered to the small intestine. The pancreas supplies digestive enzymes and bicarbonate to the same region.
The excretory system removes waste from the body, with the kidneys filtering the blood to make urine. The reproductive system, which is different in males and females, produces the new generation.

Several organs working together make an organ system. Teeth and the stomach help break food into smaller pieces and mix it, while enzymes change food molecules chemically.

board.text: Separate physical processing from chemical digestion

text.en: Incisors cut food, canines can tear and premolars and molars can crush or grind. Tooth shape helps explain the job each kind does.
A dental formula records each tooth type on one half of the upper and lower jaws. The typical adult formula including wisdom teeth gives eight teeth per side of each jaw.

board.text: Adult half-jaw: 2 incisors, 1 canine, 2 premolars, 3 molars

text.en: Saliva moistens food. Salivary amylase begins breaking down starch. Chewing helps mix food with saliva and increases the surface available for digestion.

board.text: Mouth: chewing, saliva and initial starch digestion

text.en: After swallowing, muscles in the oesophagus contract in waves. This movement, called peristalsis, pushes food toward the stomach.

board.text: Peristalsis moves food through the tract

text.en: The stomach mixes food with its secretions. Its acidic environment supports the work of pepsin, which begins breaking proteins into smaller pieces.

board.text: Stomach: mixing and some protein digestion

text.en: The duodenum is the first part of the small intestine. It receives material from the stomach along with bile and pancreatic secretions.
Bile helps disperse fat into smaller droplets. This exposes more surface where digestive enzymes can act. Bile itself does not digest fats as an enzyme.
The pancreas delivers several types of digestive enzymes. Pancreatic bicarbonate helps neutralise acid arriving from the stomach and changes conditions for those enzymes.
Different enzymes work on different molecules. Amylase acts on starch, lipase acts on fats, and proteases act on proteins. Their products can be processed further before absorption.
The inner lining of the small intestine has folds and tiny projections called villi. These increase its surface area, helping absorbed material reach blood vessels or lymph vessels.

board.text: Villi provide more surface for absorption

text.en: Many sugars and amino acids move into small blood vessels in the villi. Many digested fats follow a route through lymph vessels first.

board.text: Nutrients can enter blood or lymph

text.en: The large intestine absorbs additional water and salts. Material left over from digestion becomes faeces and leaves through the anus.

board.text: Large intestine absorbs some remaining water and salts

text.en: Removing faeces is egestion. Excretion removes waste made by body processes, such as urea. The two words describe different material leaving the body.
Lungs remove carbon dioxide during breathing. The kidneys remove certain dissolved wastes and help regulate water and salts. More than one organ contributes to excretion.

board.text: Lungs and kidneys remove different wastes

text.en: Trace the urinary system on a simple diagram. Urine forms in the kidneys, travels down the ureters, collects in the bladder and leaves through the urethra.
A nephron is a working unit of the kidney. At its beginning, pressure helps filter water and small dissolved substances from blood into a cup-shaped structure.

board.text: Nephron starts by filtering some blood contents

text.en: As the fluid travels along the nephron, much of its water and useful substances can return to the blood. This is reabsorption.

board.text: Reabsorption returns substances to the blood

text.en: Additional substances can move from blood into the tubule by secretion. Filtration, reabsorption and secretion together influence what finally leaves as urine.
The reproductive system includes organs that develop and support reproductive cells. In the basic human model, testes produce sperm and ovaries produce egg cells.

board.text: Testes produce sperm · ovaries produce egg cells

text.en: In human reproduction, a sperm and egg cell may join at fertilisation. If development continues, the uterus supports development during pregnancy.
Compare digestion and excretion by tracing what enters and exits each pathway. Digestion prepares some food molecules for absorption. The kidneys help remove waste already present in the blood.

board.text: Food breakdown and blood-waste removal have different roles

text.en: To explain an organ system, name a structure and follow the material it handles. Villi help move nutrients into the body. Nephrons help regulate which substances stay in blood or leave in urine.

board.text: Use a structure to explain the system’s job

problem.en: Why does the small intestine have folds and villi? Follow one nutrient from the gut into the body.

text.en: Identify the projections along the intestinal lining.

why.en: Villi add surface where digested molecules can pass through the lining.

text.en: Trace a digested sugar into a small blood vessel in a villus.

why.en: The blood provides a route to carry the absorbed substance to other parts of the body.

prompt.en: A friend says Absorption of digested food mainly happens in the stomach. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Most absorption happens in the small intestine.
Its long coiled shape gives a large surface.

points.en: Digestion makes food small and soluble.
The alimentary canal runs from mouth to anus.
The small intestine absorbs most digested nutrients.
